questions.stem: For data set 584, trace int s=0; for(int i=1;i<=3;i++) s+=i; what is s?

options.misconception: Reported only the final loop counter instead of the sum
The loop adds one through 3, giving the running total 6
Counted the upper bound one extra time in the total
Assumed the loop starts accumulating at zero

questions.explanation: Option B is the key because the loop adds each integer from 1 through 3 to s, producing 6 Option A fails because it reads the counter rather than the accumulated total Option C fails because it includes an iteration beyond the upper bound Option D fails because it skips the first addition in the loop.
questions.hint: Track the running sum at each iteration of the loop.

Confused dereferencing with a size query

questions.stem: For data set 586, find the bug: for (int i=0; i<=n; i++) a[i]=0; what is wrong?

options.text: The loop writes past the array end
options.misconception: The <= condition lets the index reach n, one past the last element

options.text: The index should begin at one
options.misconception: Misread zero-based indexing as starting at one
Confused assignment with equality comparison
Mistook a bounded condition for an infinite loop

questions.explanation: Option A is the key because the condition allows i to reach n, which is one past the last valid index n minus one Option B fails because arrays are zero-based, so starting at zero is correct Option C fails because a single equals sign is a valid assignment here Option D fails because the condition is bounded and will terminate normally.
questions.hint: Check the loop bound against the last valid array index.

questions.stem: For data set 587, a character array holds 6 visible letters plus a null terminator; what length does the string function report?
questions.explanation: A C string's length counts characters up to but not including the null terminator. With 6 visible letters followed by a terminator, the reported length is 6. The array itself is one byte larger because it stores that terminator.
questions.hint: Count only the visible characters, not the null terminator.

questions.stem: For data set 599, an engineer computes the C expression 31 << 2; what integer results?
questions.explanation: Shifting an integer left by two bit positions multiplies it by four. Therefore 31 << 2 equals 31 times 4, which is 124. A right shift would divide instead, and adding two would be a different operation entirely.
questions.hint: A left shift by n multiplies by two to the power of n.
